docs.title: Agent skills
docs.text:
Agent skills for teaching, by Hyun Min Kang.

  • Format: each skill is a folder with a SKILL.md in the open Agent Skills format, plus the scripts, references and examples it uses.
  • Hosts: the same folder works in Claude.ai, ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity CLI and other agents that read Agent Skills.
  • Downloads: upload-ready zips are in the repository's zip/ folder.

docs.title: Skills
docs.text: skill what it does canvas-quizbank Turns class material into a Canvas quiz item bank: a QTI .zip with math, code, tables and figures, plus a YAML source and an answer-keyed review sheet. Items are verified by running their code. See the worked example and how to import.

docs.title: Repository layout
docs.text:
skills/<name>/             one folder per skill: SKILL.md + scripts/ references/ examples/
zip/claude/<name>.zip      generated: skill folder inside the zip (Claude.ai, ChatGPT)
zip/gemini/<name>.zip      generated: SKILL.md at the zip root (Gemini)
samples/<name>/            ready-made outputs (e.g. Canvas QTI packages) for people to try
samples/<name>/<example>/  end-to-end runs: input material, prompt, and each platform's downloads
docs/                      this site; reference pages include the skills' own files
tests/                     standard-library unittest suites
tools/build_zips.py        checks, tests and zips every skill
mkdocs.yml                 site configuration
LICENSE, NOTICE            Apache 2.0 and third-party attributions

docs.title: After changing a skill
docs.text:
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests     # the tests alone
python3 tools/build_zips.py               # checks + tests, then rewrites zip/

build_zips.py refuses to write zips when a check or test fails. It checks that:

  • SKILL.md has frontmatter with a name equal to the folder name (lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, at most 64 characters);
  • the description has 1–200 characters (Claude.ai's upload limit; the open Agent Skills spec allows 1,024, but every host must accept the zip);
  • no skill folder contains a .zip (Claude.ai rejects a skill zip that contains another zip, so built packages go to samples/);
  • every file is a type Gemini accepts, or text that can be renamed with a .txt suffix in the Gemini zip (Gemini rejects other types, and the build stops on an unsupported binary);
  • the tests in tests/ pass.

The zips are deterministic (sorted entries, fixed timestamps), so they change in git only when the skill does. Commit them with the change.

docs.title: Adding a skill
docs.text:
1. Create skills/<name>/SKILL.md with name, description (what it does and when to use it, in the user's words, at most 200 characters) and license: Apache-2.0.
  2. Keep SKILL.md short; put details in references/.
  3. Put scripts in scripts/, standard library only where possible: chat sandboxes cannot install packages.
  4. Put worked examples in examples/.
  5. Add tests/test_<name>.py.
  6. Add a row to the skills table in README.md and docs/index.md, and a section to docs/ and mkdocs.yml.
  7. Run python3 tools/build_zips.py.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
pip install -r requirements-docs.txt
mkdocs serve          # preview at http://127.0.0.1:8000
mkdocs build --strict # what a deploy would run

Reference pages include the skill files with --8<-- "skills/<name>/references/<file>.md" (pymdownx.snippets). Edit the skill file, not the page, so the documentation and the agent's instructions stay identical.

docs.title: canvas-quizbank notes
docs.text:
• scripts/mdrender.py replaces Pandoc. Before it shipped, it was compared with Pandoc on 3,408 text fields from about 570 real items: the visible text, math and structure matched everywhere except choices that start with "(ii)" or "(a)". Pandoc turns those into one-item numbered lists; this renderer keeps the text as written.
  • references/canvas.md has a "Verified in Canvas" table. Update it when an import confirms or breaks a feature.

docs.title: Install a skill
docs.text:
Every skill in this repository is a folder, skills/<name>/, with a SKILL.md at its top. How you install it depends on where you use it:

  • Chat apps (Claude.ai, ChatGPT, Gemini and others): upload a zip on the app's Skills page. No terminal needed.
  • Coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity CLI, GitHub Copilot, Cursor and others): put the skill folder in the agent's skills folder.

The steps below use canvas-quizbank; for another skill, replace the name. Skill-specific requirements and a check that the install worked are on each skill's own install page, e.g. canvas-quizbank.

Menus move

These steps were checked against each product's documentation in October 2026. Vendors rename menus often; if a label differs, look for Skills in the app's settings or sidebar.

docs.title: Download the zip
docs.text:
Each skill has two zips with the same files, laid out differently because the apps disagree about the layout:

zip layout use it for zip/claude/canvas-quizbank.zip the folder canvas-quizbank/ inside the zip Claude.ai, ChatGPT, Manus; unzipping into a coding agent's skills folder zip/gemini/canvas-quizbank.zip SKILL.md at the root of the zip; some files renamed to .txt Gemini, Perplexity, Microsoft 365 Copilot Cowork

The links download the file directly. From GitHub's file page, use the Download raw file button (the arrow at the top right of the file view).

Keep the zip zipped

Safari unzips downloads by default (Safari → Settings → General → Open "safe" files after downloading). If you find a folder instead of a .zip in Downloads, turn that off and download again, rather than zipping the folder yourself: macOS adds __MACOSX/ and .DS_Store files, which some apps reject.

docs.title: Chat apps
docs.text:
Claude.aiChatGPTGemini

Works in the web app and the desktop app on every plan. On Team and Enterprise plans, an owner must allow skills and code execution for the organization (below).

  1. Turn on code execution: Settings → Capabilities → Code execution and file creation. Without it, skills are hidden.
  2. Open Customize → Skills (claude.ai/customize/skills).
  3. Click +, then Create skill → Upload a skill, and choose zip/claude/canvas-quizbank.zip.
  4. The skill appears under Your skills. Make sure its toggle is on.

Use it: start a new chat and ask in plain words; Claude loads the skill when the request matches its description. To call it by name, type / in the message box and pick the skill. Claude's thinking shows when it reads the skill.

Update: open the skill, click … → Delete, then upload the new zip.

Turn off or remove: use the toggle next to the skill, or … → Delete.

Mobile: skills you uploaded also work in the mobile apps; upload them from the web or the desktop app.

For a whole organization (Team, Enterprise):

  • An owner turns on Code execution and file creation and Skills in Organization settings → Plugins & skills → Policy.
  • To give a skill to everyone: Organization settings → Plugins & skills → Add → Upload a skill. It is on for every member, who can turn it off but not delete it.
  • A member can also share a skill they uploaded: … → Share.

Personal skills are available on ChatGPT Business, Enterprise, Edu and Healthcare, and on some personal plans. In a workspace, an admin may need to turn on skills, and Enable skill uploading, first.

  1. Go to chatgpt.com/skills. From the sidebar, the same page is under Plugins → Skills.
  2. Click Add at the top right, then Upload from your computer.
  3. Drag zip/claude/canvas-quizbank.zip into the upload box, or click the box to choose the file.
  4. ChatGPT scans the skill. Most skills are ready at once; if it shows Needs review, open it and confirm.

Use it: start a new chat (skills load when a chat starts). Ask in plain words, or type @ and pick the skill. If a skill doesn't appear in a regular chat on a Plus or Pro plan, try it in Work.

Update or remove: on the Skills page, open the skill's menu and delete it; upload the new zip to update.

Desktop and mobile: skills added in the desktop app and on the web don't sync; add the skill in each place you use it.

Use the skill in Gemini Spark, Gemini's agent mode, which runs the skill's code. Spark needs:

  • a Google AI Pro or Ultra subscription
  • a personal Google account (not work or school), age 18 or over
  • Keep Activity turned on
  • a country where Spark is offered (not the EEA, the UK, Switzerland or Nigeria)

Upload from gemini.google.com or the Mac app; the mobile apps can't upload skills.

  1. Click Settings at the bottom left of the sidebar, then Skills.
  2. Click the Upload icon at the top of the page.
  3. Drag and drop zip/gemini/canvas-quizbank.zip into the window, or click to choose it and click Open.
  4. Check the name and description Gemini read from the zip, then click Create.

Use it: click Switch to Spark in the sidebar and ask in plain words. To call the skill by name, type / (or @) and pick it.

Update: on the Skills page, open the skill, click More (⋮) → Replace skill, upload the new zip, and click Save.

Turn off or remove: More (⋮) → Deactivate stops Gemini from using it on its own; More (⋮) → Delete removes it.

Why a separate zip: Gemini needs SKILL.md at the root of the zip and accepts only certain file types (plain text such as .md, .py, .yaml, plus PDFs and images). In the Gemini zip, text files of other types get .txt appended (checks.R becomes checks.R.txt).

docs.title: Where skills go
docs.text:
Nearly every coding agent reads skills from the same two folders, with two exceptions worth knowing:

agent all projects one project Codex, GitHub Copilot, Cursor and most others ~/.agents/skills/<name>/ <project>/.agents/skills/<name>/ Claude Code ~/.claude/skills/<name>/ <project>/.claude/skills/<name>/ Antigravity CLI ~/.gemini/config/skills/<name>/ <project>/.agents/skills/<name>/

Claude Code uses the same layout with .claude in place of .agents. Antigravity reads .agents in a project but keeps skills for all projects under ~/.gemini/config/.

Committing a project's skill folder to the repository shares the skill with collaborators and with cloud agents (Claude Code on the web, the Copilot cloud agent), which see only what is in the repository.

In every case, SKILL.md must sit directly inside a folder named after the skill:

~/.agents/skills/
└── canvas-quizbank/
    ├── SKILL.md
    ├── scripts/
    ├── references/
    └── examples/

A common mistake is one level too many (~/.agents/skills/canvas-quizbank/canvas-quizbank/SKILL.md); the agent will not find that.

docs.title: Put the skill there
docs.text:
Pick one of three ways. The commands install for all projects. For one project, run them in the project folder with .agents/skills (or .claude/skills for Claude Code) in place of the folder in your home directory.

Clone and link (recommended)Download and unzip (no git)npx skills

Keep a clone of this repository and link the skill into each agent's folder. git pull then updates every agent at once.

macOS or Linux:

git clone https://github.com/hyunminkang/skills.git ~/hyunminkang-skills

# Codex, GitHub Copilot, Cursor and most other agents
mkdir -p ~/.agents/skills
ln -s ~/hyunminkang-skills/skills/canvas-quizbank ~/.agents/skills/canvas-quizbank

# Claude Code
mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills
ln -s ~/hyunminkang-skills/skills/canvas-quizbank ~/.claude/skills/canvas-quizbank

# Antigravity CLI: copy, because it may not follow links
mkdir -p ~/.gemini/config/skills
cp -R ~/hyunminkang-skills/skills/canvas-quizbank ~/.gemini/config/skills/

Windows (PowerShell; a junction needs no administrator rights):

git clone https://github.com/hyunminkang/skills.git $HOME\hyunminkang-skills

New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $HOME\.agents\skills
New-Item -ItemType Junction -Path $HOME\.agents\skills\canvas-quizbank `
  -Target $HOME\hyunminkang-skills\skills\canvas-quizbank

New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $HOME\.claude\skills
New-Item -ItemType Junction -Path $HOME\.claude\skills\canvas-quizbank `
  -Target $HOME\hyunminkang-skills\skills\canvas-quizbank

New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $HOME\.gemini\config\skills
Copy-Item -Recurse $HOME\hyunminkang-skills\skills\canvas-quizbank `
  $HOME\.gemini\config\skills\

Update later with git -C ~/hyunminkang-skills pull, then copy the Antigravity folder again.

The zip in zip/claude/ holds the folder canvas-quizbank/, so unzipping it into the skills folder gives the right layout.

macOS or Linux:

curl -LO https://github.com/hyunminkang/skills/raw/main/zip/claude/canvas-quizbank.zip

mkdir -p ~/.agents/skills ~/.claude/skills ~/.gemini/config/skills
unzip -o canvas-quizbank.zip -d ~/.agents/skills          # most agents
unzip -o canvas-quizbank.zip -d ~/.claude/skills          # Claude Code
unzip -o canvas-quizbank.zip -d ~/.gemini/config/skills   # Antigravity CLI

Windows (PowerShell):

Invoke-WebRequest -OutFile canvas-quizbank.zip `
  https://github.com/hyunminkang/skills/raw/main/zip/claude/canvas-quizbank.zip

Expand-Archive -Force canvas-quizbank.zip $HOME\.agents\skills          # most agents
Expand-Archive -Force canvas-quizbank.zip $HOME\.claude\skills          # Claude Code
Expand-Archive -Force canvas-quizbank.zip $HOME\.gemini\config\skills   # Antigravity CLI

To update, delete the canvas-quizbank folders and unzip the new zip.

skills is a command-line installer, run with Node.js, that knows the skills folder of about 85 agents.

# all projects, for Claude Code and Codex
npx skills add hyunminkang/skills --skill canvas-quizbank -g -a claude-code codex -y

# this project only; asks which agents
npx skills add hyunminkang/skills --skill canvas-quizbank
  • -g installs for all projects; without it, into the current project.
  • -a names the agents (claude-code, codex, cursor, github-copilot, opencode, …); -a '*' means all of them.
  • It keeps one copy in ~/.agents/skills/ (or .agents/skills/) and links it into the folders of agents that look elsewhere, such as ~/.claude/skills/. Add --copy to copy instead of linking.
  • npx skills list, npx skills update and npx skills remove canvas-quizbank manage what you installed.
  • For Antigravity CLI, -a antigravity-cli uses ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/skills/, which the CLI may not read; copy the skill into ~/.gemini/config/skills/ instead (see the other tabs).

Then start a new session of the agent. Most agents read skills when a session starts.

(Antigravity's skills page lists ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/skills/ for the CLI, but users report that only ~/.gemini/config/skills/ is found.)

  • Copy the folder rather than linking it: reports differ on whether Antigravity follows linked skill folders.
  • /skills reload picks up a new skill without restarting.
  • Project skills load after you answer Yes, I trust this folder.
  • Moving from Gemini CLI: project skills move from .gemini/skills/ to .agents/skills/.
all projects ~/.agents/skills/canvas-quizbank/ (also ~/.copilot/skills/) one project <project>/.agents/skills/canvas-quizbank/ (also .github/skills/, .claude/skills/) check VS Code: type /skills in Chat; Copilot CLI: /skills list call by name /canvas-quizbank

The Copilot cloud agent on github.com sees only skills committed to the repository. In the Copilot CLI, /skills reload picks up a new skill without restarting.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
The upload is rejected.

  • Check you used the right zip: Claude.ai and ChatGPT take zip/claude/; Gemini takes zip/gemini/.
  • Upload the zip as downloaded. Re-zipping on a Mac adds __MACOSX/ and .DS_Store files, which Gemini rejects.

The agent doesn't list the skill.

  • Check the path: SKILL.md must be at <skills folder>/canvas-quizbank/SKILL.md, not one folder deeper.
  • Claude Code reads .claude/skills, not .agents/skills.
  • Start a new session; most agents read skills only at the start.
  • Project skills: some agents load them only after you trust the folder.

The skill is listed twice. Agents that read both .agents/skills and .claude/skills (Cursor, Copilot, OpenCode, Amp and others) list a skill installed in both. Linking both to one clone keeps the copies identical, so either one works.

The agent ignores the skill. Call it by name (/canvas-quizbank in Claude Code and most agents, $canvas-quizbank in Codex, @ in ChatGPT), and check that its toggle is on in a chat app.

The skill's scripts fail. In a chat app, turn on code execution (Claude.ai) or use an agent mode that runs code (Gemini Spark). In a coding agent, check that python3 --version prints 3.9 or newer.

docs.title: Before installing anyone's skill
docs.text: A skill can tell the agent to run its scripts. Read SKILL.md and the scripts/ folder of any skill before installing it, as you would any program. The skills in this repository are Apache-2.0 licensed and their scripts use only the Python standard library.

docs.title: canvas-quizbank
docs.text:
Turns class material into a quiz item bank that an instructor imports into Canvas, reviews there, and trims.

Input: lecture slides, notes, PDF, PowerPoint, Word, Jupyter notebooks, Markdown (including Marp decks), LaTeX or HTML.

Output: two downloads.

download what it is <bank>.qti.zip the file to import into Canvas (New Quizzes item bank or Classic) <bank>-source-and-review.zip everything else, in one folder (below)

The second zip holds:

file what it is <bank>.yaml the source of truth; every later build and sync starts here <bank>.review.md answer-keyed review sheet; unverified items listed first <bank>.checks.R / .py the code that verified each item figures/ PNG figures used by items, if any README.md summary, unverified items, the agent's notes, import and sync steps

Keep that zip: give it back to the agent (with a Canvas export) to sync after your review, or to revise the bank later.

See it in action: a worked example (one genetics lecture, run on Claude.ai, ChatGPT and Gemini) and importing into Canvas, step by step with screenshots.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
• Reads the material and numbers every slide, page or cell, so each item records where it comes from.
  • Asks only what it needs (number of items, code languages, audience, sections), then shows a one-screen coverage plan before drafting. Saying "just build it" skips both.
  • Drafts more items than you need, all marked draft, so you can trim. Items are multiple choice by default; multiple-answer, numerical and true/false items are drafted on request.
  • Writes math and code as Canvas expects:
  • LaTeX becomes Canvas equation images, the form Canvas's own equation editor produces.
  • Code blocks, ruled tables and figures with required alt text are kept.
  • Verifies items by running them: every snippet runs as printed, every number is recomputed, and the code is kept beside the bank.
  • Learns from your review: after you delete items in Canvas, it reads a Canvas export (or a list of kept ids) and marks the YAML: kept items reviewed, deleted ones removed.

The authoring rules come from several rounds of instructor review of real banks; see the authoring guide. A course profile adds a course's own conventions.

docs.title: Status in Canvas
docs.text:
feature status multiple choice with math and code in use in a live course multiple answers, numerical, true/false confirmed by importing the smoke-test bank (2026-10-10) bundled images confirmed with the smoke-test bank (2026-10-10) ruled tables styled after the first import; re-check pending Classic objectbank mode built to Canvas's documented shape; not yet confirmed

Before your first real bank, import the smoke-test bank into a sandbox course.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Python 3.9 or newer; nothing else is required (PyYAML is bundled). Optional:

  • R or Python, to verify items that show code in that language
  • Poppler (pdftotext, pdftoppm, pdfimages), for PDF text, page images and picture detection

docs.title: Authoring guide
docs.text:
How to write items an instructor keeps. These defaults come from several rounds of instructor review of real banks. A course profile (references/profile.md) adds to them and wins when the two conflict.

Contents: 1 what an item certifies · 2 the ten default rules · 3 item styles and types · 4 stems, options, explanations · 5 difficulty · 6 the coverage plan · 7 verification and the checks file · 8 figures · 9 self-review before handing over

docs.title: 1. What an item certifies
docs.text: Ask of every draft: which idea from the material does a correct answer show the student understands? If the honest answer is "a detail of one library's API" or "that they remember the slides", drop the item.

docs.title: 2. The ten default rules
docs.text:
1. Test the core idea, not trivia. Good targets are how a method works, how its cost grows, what a key step does, and how it behaves numerically. Asking about a key step of an implementation is fine. Never test a library's calling convention, argument order, one implementation's quirks or incidental naming. When the material is about a library (a chapter on purrr, a pandas tutorial), test the ideas its functions embody (what a map returns, that a reduction carries an accumulator, that a predicate search stops early), not argument names, shortcuts or aliases.
  2. Answerable without these slides. Someone who knows the subject but never saw this material must be able to answer it. Do not use the material's private names for examples or strategies, its one-off notation, its helper-function names or its classroom analogies. Use standard terms and define every symbol in the stem. Code shown in full may define any function it needs, but give helpers generic names (my_map, f) rather than the material's.
  3. Numbers are fine; arithmetic is not the point. Concrete numbers and small examples are welcome, but any computation takes at most one or two simple mental steps (16/4, (2 − 1)/0.5). Never require a calculator, a full substitution, or more than about five quick checks.
  4. Mix the styles in every bank. Combine symbolic items (Θ(n²) in n, p, k), small concrete examples (a 2×2 matrix, five counts, a tiny graph), short code with "what does this print?" or "which line fails?", and realistic sizes where the arithmetic is mental (10,000 × 100). An all-symbolic or all-code bank is a defect.
  5. One clear question per stem. Say exactly what is compared, counted or printed ("what does the last line print?", "how many times does lm() run?"). No two-part stems. When the answer depends on what a library call does and that behavior is not what the item tests, state it in the stem ("ecdf(x) returns the empirical CDF as a function"). When the behavior is the idea being tested, do not state it; make sure it is a core idea (rule 1).
  6. Options of the same shape. Options are parallel in form and similar in length; the key is not the longest option. Put no "because ..." clause in options: reasons belong in explanation. Prefer values (outputs, numbers, Θ-classes) to prose. Avoid "all of the above" and "none of the above" unless the idea really needs it.
  7. Complete code that runs as printed. Show the whole function, not a fragment. Run every snippet exactly as printed and recompute every number in the stem, options and explanation (section 7).
  8. No hints across items; even coverage. Code or text in one item must not reveal another item's answer. Use each worked example about once. Spread items evenly over the material's sections. Do not refer to homework, exams, past terms or course-internal files.
  9. Overdraft, then let the instructor trim. Draft about 1.3× the target (e.g. 65 for a 50-item bank), with difficulty around ⅓ easy, ½ medium and the rest hard, every item status: draft, and keys spread across positions.
  10. Explanations teach. Two to four sentences: why the key is right, and what mistake leads to each tempting distractor. Canvas shows the explanation as feedback after the attempt.

docs.title: 3. Item styles and types
docs.text:
Styles (use several in every bank):

style example stem predict the output "What does the last line print?" find the change "Exactly one of these one-line changes makes it return 4. Which?" find the error "Exactly one row of the table is wrong. Which one?" cost "What is the total cost of the factory call and the k calls?" (Θ) apply the idea to a new case "Which value can b() never return?" read a figure "Which statement about the counts must be true?" property "Which term can be dropped without moving the maximum?"

Types. Use multiple choice unless the instructor or profile asks for others, or the request says "mix in other types". When other types are allowed:

  • numerical: the answer is one number a student can get in one or two mental steps (an estimate, a count, a probability). Give a tolerance or a range that accepts reasonable rounding, and say in the stem how many decimals to enter.
  • multiple_answers: "select all that apply" over 4 or 5 statements with 2 or 3 correct. Every statement is independently checkable.
  • true_false: only for a clean, important statement. Use sparingly (at most about 1 in 20); true/false is the easiest type to guess.

Canvas has more types (matching, fill in the blank); this skill does not build them.

docs.title: 4. Stems, options, explanations
docs.text:
• Stem. Put the setup (code, formula, table, figure) first and the question last, as its own short paragraph. Name variables generically (x, f, fit), not after the lecture's examples. Fix nuisance parameters so a Θ is in one variable.
  • Distractors come from real mistakes: the off-by-one count, forgetting to divide by λ, the shared-state assumption, the value before an update, n instead of n − 1. Every distractor must be clearly wrong to someone who understands; if an expert could argue for it, rewrite it.
  • Options are 4 for multiple choice (3 is the minimum). Order numeric options naturally or at random; the build keeps your order and Canvas shuffles when shuffle_answers: true (the default).
  • Explanation. Say why the key is right, then name the mistake behind the main distractors. Do not restate the question.
  • Formatting. Code in fenced blocks with a language (```r, ```python), math in $...$ and $$...$$, tables as pipe tables. See schema.md for the supported Markdown.

docs.title: 5. Difficulty
docs.text:
• easy: one idea, applied directly (predict a short output, recognize a definition in use).
  • medium: one idea applied to a case the material did not show, or two ideas combined in one short step.
  • hard: a subtle consequence (lazy evaluation in a loop, what memory a closure keeps, a cost that changes with where work happens), still answerable in about two minutes.

Hard never means long, tricky wording or heavy arithmetic.

docs.title: 6. The coverage plan
docs.text:
Show this to the instructor before drafting, on one screen:

Bank: <title>                       Target: 50 kept → draft 65
Source: lecture09.pptx (155 slides), notes09.pdf (12 pages)
Languages: R, Python                Types: multiple choice only

section (source)                  objectives                         items  e/m/h
Seeds and generators (sl. 4-20)   seeds, period, Lehmer generator       8   3/4/1
Inverse transform (sl. 21-35)     continuous, discrete, Box-Muller      9   3/5/1
...
Total                                                                  65  22/32/11

Figures: 3 (a histogram, two density sketches). Not covered: <sections and why>.

Wait for an OK or edits. On "just build it", skip the plan and use the defaults.

docs.title: 7. Verification and the checks file
docs.text:
• Run every code snippet as printed, in its own language. Recompute every number in stems, options and explanations. Check that each distractor is wrong.
  • Save the code you ran next to the bank as <bank>.checks.R and/or <bank>.checks.py. It runs top to bottom, stops at the first failed check, and has one section per item, headed # ---- <id>. The validator warns when a verified: run item has no section. Wrap each section so one item's objects cannot change another's result:
# <bank>.checks.R — run: Rscript <bank>.checks.R
check <- function(id, ok) {
  if (!isTRUE(ok)) stop("check failed: ", id, call. = FALSE)
  cat("ok", id, "\n")
}
cat(R.version.string, "\n")            # record versions of what you use
# ---- ff-004: two counters
local({
  ...code exactly as printed in the item...
  check("ff-004", identical(c(a(), a(), b(), a()), c(1, 2, 1, 3)))
})
cat("all checks passed\n")

# <bank>.checks.py — run: python3 <bank>.checks.py
import sys
def check(item_id, ok):
    if not ok:
        sys.exit(f"check failed: {item_id}")
    print("ok", item_id)
print(sys.version)
# ---- ff-004: two counters
def _ff_004():
    ...code exactly as printed in the item...
    check("ff-004", result == [1, 2, 1, 3])
_ff_004()
print("all checks passed")

When an item's answer depends on a fresh session (for example "object not found"), run that snippet on its own as well (Rscript --vanilla -e '...', python3 -I -c '...'). - Packages: load them in the section that uses them and print their versions. If a package the item needs is missing and cannot be installed, either rewrite the item with base functions (when the idea does not depend on the package) or mark it verified: no with the reason. - Set verified: run only if the item's checks ran and passed. Otherwise set verified: no and a verify_note saying why ("R not available in this sandbox", "conceptual: nothing to execute"). Never "verify" R code by translating it to Python: random streams, integer types and printing differ between languages, and those are often what the item tests. - A conceptual item with nothing to run can still check its numbers (a formula evaluated at the stem's values). - Do not ask for the values of a language's own random generator unless the seed and generator are fixed in the stem and the item says which language; R and NumPy give different draws for the same seed.

docs.title: 8. Figures
docs.text:
• Use a figure only when the picture carries the idea (a curve's shape, a histogram's skew, a matrix's sparsity pattern). If a table or printed output says the same thing, use that.
  • Draw with R (png(..., width = 640, height = 400, res = 110)) or matplotlib (figsize=(6.4, 4), dpi=100). Keep text at least 10 pt and labels on the axes. Do not encode meaning by color alone.
  • Save as PNG under figures/ next to the YAML, and keep the drawing code in the checks file.
  • Alt text (required) describes what a student needs to answer: the axes, the shape and any marked values. It may contain the value a sighted student reads off the figure; it must not contain the conclusion the item asks for.
  • To reuse a figure from the material, take it from the extractor's media/ folder (a PPTX picture or a rendered PDF page), cropped to the figure.

docs.title: 9. Self-review before handing over
docs.text:
Run this over the whole bank, not only the newest items:

  • [ ] validate_bank.py --require-source --report shows 0 errors; warnings are read and either fixed or explained.
  • [ ] Every item's source points at a real slide, page or section.
  • [ ] Key positions are spread out; the report's "key clearly the longest option" list is short (it is informational; when the long key is unavoidable, e.g. an option describing an error, say so in the hand-over).
  • [ ] No item uses a name or symbol the stem does not define.
  • [ ] No two items test the same example the same way, and no item answers another.
  • [ ] Every verified: no has a reason, and they are listed for the instructor.
  • [ ] The styles of section 3 are mixed.

docs.title: Which package to build
docs.text:
goal build with import path New Quizzes item bank (most courses) --mode assessment (default) Item Banks (course navigation, or Manage Item Banks from a New Quiz) → + Bank → name it → open the bank → ⋮ → Import Content → upload the zip Classic Quizzes question bank --mode objectbank Course Settings → Import Course Content → QTI .zip file → the items arrive as a question bank named after title Classic quiz --mode assessment the same Settings import path; arrives as an unpublished quiz

To give the bank a clear name in Canvas, set title: in the YAML before building.

docs.title: What the instructor sees
docs.text:
• Title: each item is titled <id> · <title> (e.g. ff-004 · Two counters), so items can be found, discussed and synced by id. --no-id-in-title turns this off.
  • Question and choices: the rendered Markdown. Math appears as Canvas equation images and code in monospace blocks.
  • Feedback: the explanation, plus a final line "Source: ...". Students see it after submitting, as the quiz settings allow.
  • Options are shuffled per student when shuffle_answers: true.

docs.title: The review loop
docs.text:
1. Import the package and read the items in Canvas; delete the ones that do not fit. The review sheet (<bank>.review.md, answers marked ✅, unverified items listed first) is the same content offline.
  2. Export what is left:
  3. a New Quizzes quiz that uses the bank: the quiz's menu → Export (QTI)
  4. Classic: Settings → Export Course Content (choose the quiz or bank), which downloads an .imscc
  5. if no export is available: copy the remaining item titles (each starts with its id) into a text file, one per line
  6. Run sync_from_canvas.py BANK.yaml --export export.zip (or --kept-ids kept.txt). Read the dry run, then add --write. Kept items become reviewed, deleted ones removed. Items edited in Canvas are listed so the edit can be copied into the YAML by hand.
  7. Rebuild with --reviewed-only when a clean, reviewed-only package is needed.

docs.title: Package format (what Canvas enforces)
docs.text:
build_qti.py writes imsmanifest.xml, assessment.xml and images/*. These details each cost a failed import; validate_bank.py --qti checks them all:

  • Bare default namespaces. <manifest xmlns="...">, never <ns0:manifest>. Canvas finds the QTI resource with CSS selectors that do not match prefixed elements and reports only "Unsupported content package".
  • Equation images, never MathML. New Quizzes renders MathML as "Unexpected text node: ''".
  • Feedback before scoring. The continue="Yes" feedback condition comes before the continue="No" scoring condition. Otherwise students who answer correctly never see the explanation.
  • Images go under images/, each declared as a webcontent resource in the manifest, and are referenced as %24IMS-CC-FILEBASE%24/images/<name>, the layout Canvas's own exports use. Canvas copies them into the course files on import. --image-mode inline embeds data: URIs instead, as a fallback.

docs.title: Importing into Canvas
docs.text: Import the <bank>.qti.zip download. The other zip (-source-and-review) is for you and the agent; Canvas does not use it.

docs.title: New Quizzes item bank (recommended)
docs.text:
1. Create a new item bank. Open Item Banks (from the course navigation, or Manage Item Banks from a New Quiz). Choose + Bank, name the bank, and choose Create Bank. Importing each package into its own new bank keeps its items together and easy to review.

2. Import the package. Open the new bank, choose the ⋮ menu at the top right, then Import Content, and upload <bank>.qti.zip. The import can take a minute.

3. Review the items.

  • Each item's title starts with its id (here hwe-026 · A single copy of the minor allele), so you can find it in the review sheet and tell the agent which items you kept.
  • Math is rendered by Canvas, code appears in monospace blocks, and the figures come with the package.

Delete the items that don't fit, using the trash icon on each item. Then build quizzes from the bank, for example by drawing a set number of random items per attempt.

docs.title: Classic Quizzes
docs.text:
Course Settings → Import Course Content → content type QTI .zip file, and upload the package.

  • By default the items arrive as a quiz.
  • For a named question bank, ask the agent to package with --mode objectbank.

docs.title: After your review
docs.text:
Give the agent the -source-and-review.zip and one of:

  • a Canvas export of what is left
  • a text file of the remaining item titles, one per line

It marks the kept items reviewed and the deleted ones removed, then hands back a fresh pair of downloads. Removed ids are never reused, so deleted items never come back. See Using the skill.

docs.title: Course profile
docs.text:
A course profile records one course's conventions, so every bank for that course follows them without the instructor repeating themselves. It is an optional YAML file, usually quizbank_profile.yaml next to the course material or the banks. The instructor may also paste it into the chat.

Precedence: the instructor's request, then the profile, then the defaults in authoring-guide.md. A profile rule that conflicts with a default replaces it; everything else adds to it.

course: "STAT 101: Introduction to Statistics"
audience: "first-year undergraduates; no programming before this course"
languages: [R]               # languages items may show code in; [] = no code
types: [multiple_choice]     # allowed types (default: multiple_choice only)
bank:
  target_items: 50           # items wanted after the instructor trims
  overdraft: 1.3             # draft target × overdraft (default 1.3)
  difficulty_mix: {easy: 0.33, medium: 0.5, hard: 0.17}
  id_prefix: "w05-"          # ids are prefix + 3 digits: w05-001, w05-002, ...
  points: 1
notation:                    # how to write things
  - "Write sample means as \\overline{x}, never \\bar{x}."
avoid:                       # never include
  - "Questions about the textbook's chapter numbering."
rules:                       # extra rules, in the instructor's words
  - "Every item about a test names the null hypothesis."

Every field is optional. Unknown fields are allowed: read them as instructions.

docs.title: When there is no profile
docs.text: Ask only what the request does not answer (see SKILL.md, intake). At the end, offer to save the answers as quizbank_profile.yaml for next time, and write it only if the instructor agrees.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
• examples/profiles/template.yaml: every field, commented
  • examples/profiles/bios615.yaml: a graduate statistical computing course with R and Python, showing many real conventions

# the skill's default rules (references/authoring-guide.md).

  target_items: 50    # items wanted after the instructor trims
  overdraft: 1.3      # how many times the target to draft
  difficulty_mix: {easy: 0.33, medium: 0.5, hard: 0.17}
  id_prefix: ""       # e.g. "w05-" gives w05-001, w05-002, ...

docs.title: A worked example: a graduate statistical computing course
docs.text:
# Profile for a graduate statistical computing course (BIOSTAT 615, University
# of Michigan, Fall 2026). The rules below came out of the instructor's reviews
# of about 500 drafted review-bank items.

course: "BIOSTAT 615: AI-assisted Statistical Programming"
audience: >
  Biostatistics MS and PhD students who program in R and Python and know
  introductory probability, linear models and linear algebra.

languages: [R, Python]
types: [multiple_choice]

bank:
  target_items: 50
  overdraft: 1.4        # the instructor asked for 60-80 drafts per topic to trim
  difficulty_mix: {easy: 0.33, medium: 0.5, hard: 0.17}
  id_prefix: "t{topic}-"   # t9-001 for topic 9
  points: 1

notation:
  - "Covariance matrices are V (V1, V^{-1}), never Sigma: Σ reads as a summation."
  - "Sample means are \\overline{X} and \\overline{x}, not \\bar{X}."
  - "Definitions and formulas use symbols (a threshold t, a correlation rho); a number appears only beside a computed result ('for t = 5: ...')."
  - "Complexity is stated in Θ() notation ('runs in Θ(n²); which change makes it Θ(n)?'), with nuisance parameters fixed so Θ is in one variable."
  - "Relative error is the average of |estimate/θ − 1|, reported to 3 significant digits; never relative RMSE."
  - "Importance sampling: do not call anything a 'weight'; state the averaged quantity (f(X)/q(X)) explicitly."
  - "Numbers in one table or list share one precision."

avoid:
  - "Any mention of a past term or past offering of the course, in items, explanations or code comments."
  - "Questions or explanations that refer to a homework, its solutions or its function names."
  - "Values drawn from R's or NumPy's own generators: the same seed gives different draws. Use supplied uniforms, a hand-written generator, or seed-free statistics."
  - "In banks that feed an exam: Union-Find items and items on AI-assisted coding tools."
  - "More than about two numerical-precision items per bank."

rules:
  - "Prefer small traceable inputs (fib_memo(5), not fib_memo(30) with a memorized formula)."
  - "When code is shown, it is complete and generic in naming; a question about a library call states what the call does."
  - "Rejected styles from past reviews: counting loop iterations, Strassen call counts, by-hand LU/Cholesky/QR steps, timing extrapolation in seconds, more than two traces of one worked example."

docs.title: Rejected patterns, with fixes
docs.text: Each pair shows an item an instructor rejected in review and the version that replaced it. All are on the Advanced R function-factories material, so they can be compared with advanced-r-function-factories/.

docs.title: 1. Trivia instead of the idea
docs.text:
Rejected: it tests where a helper lives, not what a closure does.

question: |
  Which package provides `env_print()`, used to inspect a function's
  enclosing environment?
choices: ['rlang', 'base', 'pryr', 'lobstr']

Fixed: ask what the idea predicts for concrete code (see ff-001).

question: |
  ```r
  power <- function(exp) {
    function(x) x^exp
  }
  square <- power(2)
  cube <- power(3)
  c(square(4), cube(2))
  ```

  What does the last line print?
choices: ['`64 8`', '`16 8`', '`16 16`', '`Error: object ''exp'' not found`']

docs.title: 2. Names that only the lecture uses
docs.text:
Rejected: "the promise trap" and "the slide-12 factory" mean nothing to someone who learned the topic elsewhere.

question: |
  Why does the slide-12 factory fall into the promise trap?

Fixed: show the code and ask what it prints (see ff-002). Use standard terms such as "lazy evaluation", and define any symbol in the stem.

docs.title: 3. Arithmetic instead of understanding
docs.text:
Rejected: computing ℓ(3) to three decimals takes a calculator and tests arithmetic, not likelihood.

question: |
  For x = (2, 4, 3, 7) and a Poisson model, compute ℓ(3) to three decimals.
type: numerical

Fixed: ask for the maximizer, one or two mental steps once the idea is known (see ff-010: $\hat\lambda = \bar{x} = 16/4$).

docs.title: 4. Options that give the key away
docs.text:
Rejected: only the key carries a justification, and it is by far the longest option.

choices:
  - '`8`, because the promise is evaluated when `square()` is first called and `e` is 3 by then'
  - '`4`'
  - '`9`'
  - 'an error'

Fixed: options are values of the same form, and the reasoning moves to explanation.

choices: ['`4`', '`9`', '`8`', '`Error: object ''e'' not found`']

docs.title: 5. Two questions in one stem
docs.text:
Rejected: "and" asks two things, so a partly right answer has no option.

question: |
  What does `c(a(), a(), b(), a())` print, and how many environments
  does the code create?

Fixed: one question ("What does the last line print?", ff-004). If the second part matters, it gets its own item.

docs.title: 6. A fragment instead of complete code
docs.text:
Rejected: the factory is not shown, so the answer depends on a guess.

question: |
  After `a <- new_counter()`, what does `c(a(), a(), a())` print?

Fixed: show the complete, runnable code (ff-004 and ff-005 each show the whole factory), and run it as printed before shipping.

docs.title: 7. "Why" with prose options
docs.text:
Rejected: prose explanations as options invite arguments about wording, and several can be partly right.

question: Why does the counter made with `<-` not count?
choices:
  - 'Because `<-` creates a local variable that is discarded'
  - 'Because R copies the environment on every call'
  - 'Because the factory returns before the counter runs'
  - 'Because `i` is a promise'

Fixed: ask what happens instead ("What does the last line print?", ff-005), and put the reason in explanation.

docs.title: 8. One question answering another
docs.text:
Rejected: an item whose code fixes the bug with force(exp) and prints 4, in the same bank as ff-002, which asks what the unfixed code prints. Drawn into one quiz, the first gives away the second.

Fixed: test each example once; when two items share code, neither may show the other's answer.

docs.title: Bank schema
docs.text:
A bank is one YAML file: a title, a description, and a list of questions. scripts/validate_bank.py enforces everything below.

title: "Example Bank: Function Factories in R"   # Canvas shows it as the bank/quiz name
description: |                                    # for people; not exported
  Where the items come from, how they were checked, how to build.
questions:
  - id: ff-004                    # unique, never reused; letters, digits, . _ -
    topic: function-factories     # optional free tag
    objective: state              # learning objective tag; the report counts these
    difficulty: medium            # easy | medium | hard
    status: draft                 # draft | reviewed | removed (default draft)
    source: "Advanced R (2e) §10.2.4"   # where in the material; shown in feedback
    verified: run                 # run | no
    verify_note: "..."            # required when verified: no
    title: "Two counters"         # short name; Canvas title becomes "ff-004 · Two counters"
    type: multiple_choice         # see "Types" (default multiple_choice)
    points: 1                     # default 1
    shuffle_answers: true         # default true (choice types only)
    question: |                   # Markdown + $TeX$; see "Markdown"
      ...
    choices: [...]                # choice types only
    answer: 3                     # form depends on type
    explanation: |                # Markdown; Canvas general feedback
      ...

Required: id, objective, difficulty, question, answer, explanation; choices for the choice types. source is required for new drafts (--require-source). The validator warns without it, so older banks still build.

docs.title: Types
docs.text:
type choices answer Canvas type multiple_choice 3+ distinct zero-based index: 2 multiple choice multiple_answers 3+ distinct list of indexes: [0, 2] multiple answers (Canvas's own scoring; partial credit is a quiz setting) numerical none {value: 4, tolerance: 0.01} or {min: 0.97, max: 0.98} numerical true_false none true or false true/false

tolerance is absolute: {value: 2.082, tolerance: 0.001} accepts 2.081 through 2.083.

docs.title: Status
docs.text:
• draft: written by the agent and not yet reviewed (every new item)
  • reviewed: kept by the instructor (set by hand or by sync_from_canvas.py)
  • removed: deleted in review. The item stays in the file so its id is never reused, but it is never built, and the validator skips its content checks.

build_qti.py --reviewed-only packages only reviewed items.

docs.title: Markdown
docs.text:
question, choices and explanation are Markdown, rendered by scripts/mdrender.py (standard library only):

  • Paragraphs are separated by a blank line. Emphasis uses *em*, **strong**, ~~strike~~, ^sup^ and ~sub~.
  • Code: inline code, and fenced blocks with an optional language: ```r, ```python, ```{r}, or ~~~.
  • Math: $inline$ and $$display$$ TeX in standard amsmath (\frac, \sum, \overline, \begin{pmatrix}, ...). A $ opens math only before a non-space, and closes only after a non-space when no digit follows, so $5 and $20 stays text. Write a literal dollar as \$.
  • Tables are pipe tables with an optional alignment row (:--, :-:, --:). Cells may hold code and math; a | inside $...$ or backticks does not split a cell. They render with a ruled grid, padded cells and a shaded header row (inline styles, since Canvas adds none).
  • Lists use -, * or 1.; nested items are indented two or more spaces.
  • Images: ![alt text](figures/name.png), with the path relative to the YAML file; PNG, JPEG or GIF. Alt text is required.
  • Other blocks: links, > blockquotes, headings and --- rules.
  • Typography: outside code and math, quotes become curly, -- becomes an en dash, --- an em dash and ... an ellipsis.

What is not supported:

  • Raw HTML. Only <br>, <sup>, <sub>, <kbd>, <u>, <mark> and <small> pass through. Anything else is shown as text.
  • Footnotes, definition lists and attributes on blocks.

Blank line before a block. A list, table, blockquote or heading needs a blank line before it. Without one, a wrapped line that happens to start with "3." stays text. The validator warns when a line that looks like a list item follows a text line. A fenced code block may follow text directly.

Math rendering in Canvas. Each formula becomes a Canvas equation image (/equation_images/<TeX>), the same form Canvas's own equation editor produces, rendered by the Canvas server that imports it. Never MathML: New Quizzes shows MathML as "Unexpected text node". Keep TeX standard: no \newcommand, no packages beyond amsmath.

docs.title: YAML pitfalls
docs.text:
• Use block scalars (|) for any multi-line text and for anything that contains code.
  • Quote a one-line string that contains :, starts with a backtick, *, &, !, %, @, [, {, or is yes/no/true/false.
  • Prefer single quotes for choices: backslashes stay literal ('$\lambda = 1$'). Inside single quotes, write a quote as '' ('Error: object ''x'' not found').
  • Never put TeX in double quotes: YAML treats \l, \T, ... as escape sequences, so the file fails to load or the TeX is corrupted.
  • Edit banks with exact-string edits, never multi-line regex replacements, which can silently move lines between items. Re-run the validator after every edit.

docs.title: Scripts
docs.text: The agent runs these for you, but they also work by hand. They live in skills/canvas-quizbank/scripts/ and need only Python 3.9 or newer; PyYAML is bundled in scripts/_vendor/ for environments without it. Every script prints its options with --help.

docs.title: package_bank.py
docs.text:
The usual last step: validates the bank, builds the Canvas package, checks it against the YAML, writes the review sheet, and bundles everything else.

python3 scripts/package_bank.py bank.yaml --out downloads/ --notes notes.md
  • Output: downloads/bank.qti.zip (import into Canvas) and downloads/bank-source-and-review.zip. The second zip is a folder bank/ with the YAML, the review sheet, the checks files, the figures the items use, and a README (summary, unverified items, notes, import and sync steps). It unzips into a folder whose YAML rebuilds as is.
  • Options: --notes FILE adds Markdown notes to the README; --mode, --image-mode and --reviewed-only work as in build_qti.py.
  • Nothing is written if validation or the package check fails.

docs.title: extract_material.py
docs.text:
Turns class material into one numbered outline for drafting.

python3 scripts/extract_material.py lecture.pptx notes.pdf -o work/extracted
  • Output: work/extracted/outline.md and work/extracted/media/<file>/.
  • Inputs:
type what is extracted .pptx slide titles, bullets with levels, tables, speaker notes, pictures, hidden-slide flags .docx headings, paragraphs, lists, tables, pictures; equations as plain text .ipynb Markdown cells; code cells with their language; text and image outputs .md, .Rmd, .qmd as is; Marp decks are split into slides, with <!-- notes --> listed .html text, code, lists and tables; KaTeX and MathJax v2 math recovered as $TeX$ .tex as is; Beamer decks split by frame .pdf per-page text (pdftotext or pypdf); pages with pictures are flagged
  • Options:
option effect -o DIR output folder (default extracted) --pages-png [--dpi N] render PDF pages to PNG, to crop figures from --pdf-images save the pictures embedded in a PDF

docs.title: validate_bank.py
docs.text:
Checks banks against the schema, and optionally the built package against its bank. Exits 1 on any error.

python3 scripts/validate_bank.py bank.yaml --require-source --report
python3 scripts/validate_bank.py bank.yaml --qti bank.qti.zip
option effect --report coverage summary: difficulty, types, status, key positions, objectives --require-source a missing source is an error (use for new drafts) --qti ZIP open the package and check its manifest, namespaces, images, and every item's type and answer key against the YAML --reviewed-only with --qti, for a package built with --reviewed-only --strict treat warnings as errors --verbose list every warning instead of grouping them

docs.title: build_qti.py
docs.text:
Builds the Canvas package and, optionally, the review sheet. The bank is validated first; any error stops the build.

python3 scripts/build_qti.py bank.yaml -o bank.qti.zip --review-md bank.review.md
option effect -o ZIP output file (default: bank.qti.zip next to the YAML) --review-md FILE also write the answer-keyed review sheet --mode assessment default; for New Quizzes item banks, or a quiz in Classic --mode objectbank a named question bank in Classic Quizzes --reviewed-only package only status: reviewed items --no-id-in-title titles without the id prefix (sync then matches by text) --image-mode inline embed figures as data: URIs instead of bundling files

docs.title: sync_from_canvas.py
docs.text:
Records a review done in Canvas: kept items become reviewed, the others removed. It runs as a dry run unless --write is given.

python3 scripts/sync_from_canvas.py bank.yaml --export canvas-export.zip
python3 scripts/sync_from_canvas.py bank.yaml --kept-ids kept.txt --write
  • --export: any zip Canvas produces (a QTI quiz export, or a Classic .imscc course export); the option can be repeated.
  • --kept-ids: a text file with one id or one Canvas title per line.
  • Matching: items are matched by the id at the start of their title, and by question text when a title has no id.
  • Reported: items added in Canvas and items whose text was edited there.
  • With --write: only status: lines change and a .bak copy is kept. The file is re-read to confirm that nothing else changed; if anything did, the original is restored.

docs.title: mdrender.py
docs.text: The Markdown and math renderer behind build_qti.py, using only the standard library. The supported Markdown is listed in the schema. python3 scripts/mdrender.py < item.md prints the HTML Canvas will receive.

docs.title: Smoke test: one Canvas import
docs.text: Six items that exercise every question type and display feature. Import them once into a sandbox course to confirm that the package format works on your Canvas instance.

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
The skill holds only the source (smoke-test.yaml, figures/, the checks file and the review sheet). Skill zips cannot contain zips, so the ready-made packages are in the repository's samples/canvas-quizbank/:

  • smoke-test.qti.zip: default build (assessment mode, images bundled)
  • smoke-test.objectbank.qti.zip: objectbank mode, for Classic Quizzes question banks
  • smoke-test.inline-images.qti.zip: images embedded as data: URIs, a fallback if bundled images do not show

Or ask the agent to build the smoke test, or build it yourself:

python3 ../../scripts/build_qti.py smoke-test.yaml -o <out>/smoke-test.qti.zip
python3 ../../scripts/build_qti.py smoke-test.yaml -o <out>/smoke-test.objectbank.qti.zip --mode objectbank
python3 ../../scripts/build_qti.py smoke-test.yaml -o <out>/smoke-test.inline-images.qti.zip --image-mode inline

docs.title: Import
docs.text:
• New Quizzes: open Item Banks, choose + Bank to create a bank, open it, choose ⋮ → Import Content, and upload smoke-test.qti.zip.
  • Classic Quizzes: go to Settings → Import Course Content, choose QTI .zip file, and upload smoke-test.objectbank.qti.zip (for a question bank) or smoke-test.qti.zip (for a quiz).

docs.title: What to check
docs.text:
item type look for st-001 multiple choice display formula with a fraction and a sum; R and Python code blocks in monospace; choices rendered as math st-002 multiple answers checkboxes, not radio buttons; math in each choice; choosing A and B scores full marks st-003 numerical an answer box; 2.081, 2.082 and 2.083 score, 2.08 does not st-004 numerical (range) any value from 0.97 to 0.98 scores st-005 true/false two options, True and False; False scores st-006 multiple choice the histogram shows (not a broken image); a two-row table with a ruled grid and a shaded header; math in the table

On every item:

  • The title starts with the id (st-001 · ...).
  • After answering, the feedback shows the explanation and the source line.

If an image is broken, re-import with smoke-test.inline-images.qti.zip, then build your banks with --image-mode inline. Record what worked in references/canvas.md under "Verified in Canvas".

docs.title: Using the skill
docs.text:
Talk to the agent in plain words; it picks one of four starting points.

you say what happens "Make a quiz bank from lecture07.pptx and notes07.pdf." a new bank, all steps below "Build week5.yaml into a Canvas QTI file." validate, build, check the package "Add 10 numerical items on the bootstrap to topic09.yaml." revise: new ids continue the numbering; existing items are kept "I deleted the weak items in Canvas; here is the export." sync: kept items become reviewed, deleted ones removed

docs.title: A new bank, step by step
docs.text:
1. Profile. If a quizbank_profile.yaml is near the material (or pasted in the chat), the agent follows it. See Course profiles.
  2. Extract. The agent turns the material into one numbered outline (slides, pages, cells), with speaker notes and images in place. PDF pages whose diagrams or code exist only as pictures are flagged, so the agent looks at them directly.
  3. Questions. In one message, the agent asks only what it doesn't know:
  4. how many items you want to keep (default 50, so it drafts about 65)
  5. which code languages items may use
  6. who the audience is
  7. which sections to include or skip
  8. Coverage plan. A one-screen table of sections, objectives, item counts and difficulty. Reply "OK" or edit it.
  9. Draft section by section, following the authoring guide.
  10. Verify. Every snippet runs as printed and every number is recomputed. The code is saved as <bank>.checks.R / .py. Items that cannot be run in this environment (for example R in a chat sandbox) are marked verified: no with the reason.
  11. Validate the bank.
  12. Package it as two files: <bank>.qti.zip (checked against the YAML) and <bank>-source-and-review.zip (YAML, review sheet, checks, figures and a README).
  13. Hand over the two downloads, with counts by section, difficulty and type, the unverified items, and the import steps.

"Just build it" skips steps 3 and 4 and uses the defaults.

docs.title: Downloading in a chat
docs.text:
The agent offers exactly two files:

product how the files appear Claude.ai as download cards under the reply ChatGPT as links in the reply Gemini as downloadable files in the reply

Import the .qti.zip into Canvas. Open the other zip for the review sheet, and keep it: the agent needs its YAML for any later change or sync.

docs.title: Reviewing in Canvas
docs.text:
1. Import the .qti.zip (how).
  2. Read the items in Canvas and delete the ones that don't fit.
  3. Each title starts with the item's id, e.g. ff-004 · Two counters.
  4. Each explanation ends with the item's source, e.g. "Source: slides 41–43".
  5. The .review.md sheet has the same items with answers marked, for reading offline.
  6. Give the agent the -source-and-review.zip plus a Canvas export of what's left, or a text file of the remaining titles. It shows a dry run, updates the YAML, and hands back a fresh pair of downloads. Items you edited in Canvas are listed so the edits can be copied into the YAML.

Deleted items stay in the YAML as status: removed, so their ids are never reused and they never come back in a rebuild.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Name the files and the folder you want; otherwise the agent uses quizbank/<bank-name>/.
  • Say "multiple choice only" or "mix in numerical items" to control types.
  • Put lasting preferences (languages, audience, notation, things to avoid) in a profile once instead of repeating them; the agent offers to save them after a first bank.
  • Review the "Check these first" list at the top of the review sheet: unverified items and items without a source.
